rules.head: Blocked by Open Machine on prod-us-01
rules.foot: Do not try another way. An admin of Acme Robotics can change this in Rules.

commands.title: system-folders
commands.note: This would delete, or change who owns, a folder that the system or a whole home lives in. Remove only the exact files or folders you made, by their full path.

commands.title: disks
commands.note: This would erase a disk or change how it is divided. To look at disks, use lsblk, fdisk -l or diskutil list.

commands.title: power
commands.note: This would turn the machine off or restart it, and nobody could reach it until a person turns it on. To restart one service, restart that service.

commands.title: disconnect
commands.note: This would stop Open Machine, every process of its user or the machine’s network, and nobody could connect to it again. To signal one process, give its ID and name the signal, as in kill -HUP 1234. If the network needs a change, tell the person.

commands.title: accounts
commands.note: This would add, remove or change an account that can sign in to the machine. Tell the person which account change you need.

commands.title: saved-passwords
commands.note: This would print a password or token the machine keeps for another service. Run the tool itself (gh, aws, gcloud, kubectl): it uses its saved sign-in without showing it.

commands.title: scheduled-jobs
commands.note: This would delete all of the user’s scheduled jobs at once. To change one, save crontab -l to a file, edit it, and run crontab with that file.

commands.title: delete-folders
commands.note: On this machine, deleting a folder and everything in it is blocked. Tell the person which folder you want removed.

commands.title: administrator
commands.note: On this machine, commands that ask for administrator power are blocked. Run it without that, or tell the person what needs it.

commands.title: remote-scripts
commands.note: On this machine, running a script straight from the internet is blocked. Save it to a file, tell the person what it does, and run it only when they agree.

commands.title: git-history
commands.note: This would overwrite or delete work that is already saved in Git. Make a new commit or a new branch instead, or tell the person.

commands.title: cloud-resources
commands.note: This would remove servers, storage or a whole environment in a cloud account, or local containers and their data. Show the person the plan and let them run the removal.

commands.title: databases
commands.note: This would delete a database or everything in one of its tables. Tell the person what you want removed and let them run it.

commands.title: publishing
commands.note: This would release software to the public under the owner’s name. Prepare the release and let the person publish it.

files.title: secrets
files.note: These files hold passwords, tokens and private keys. The tools that use them still work: git, ssh, aws, kubectl, your app, and flags such as --env-file. Do not print, copy, change or upload them; if one must be made or changed, tell the person what to put in it. Example files (.env.example) and public keys (*.pub) are open.

files.title: saved-data
files.note: These hold saved passwords, browser sign-ins and the commands typed before. Nothing in an ordinary task needs them.

files.title: open-machine
files.note: These are Open Machine’s own settings and keys. Nothing in a task needs them.

files.title: sign-in
files.note: These files decide who can sign in and what runs when they do, before every command. You can read them. To change one, tell the person the exact lines.

files.title: git-settings
files.note: These are the settings and scripts Git runs by itself. You can read them. Use the repository as it is set up, or tell the person what you would change.

files.title: ai-settings
files.note: These files tell AI tools and editors what they may do. You can read them. Tell the person what you would change.

files.title: release-settings
files.note: These files build, test and release the project. You can read them. On this machine, tell the person what you would change.
